trigger: do_tick/1 called on a healthy N-node cluster where DNS/static resolution returns this node's own address alongside peers
summary: peers_resolved counted node()'s own resolved address while peers_connected (nodes()) never includes self, so the shipped YuzuGatewayClusterPartiallyFormed alert fired permanently on every healthy multi-node cluster. Empirically reproduced with a real 3-container Docker Compose scale group.

trigger: scripts/integration-test.sh Phase-4-reuse mode run after vm.args.src's node short-name rename (yuzu_gw1 -> yuzu_gw)
summary: The Phase-4-reuse GATEWAY_PID pgrep pattern hardcoded the retired 'yuzu_gw1@127.0.0.1' node name; vm.args.src's rename to a shared 'yuzu_gw@<addr>' short name broke it silently. Independently found by architect, gateway-erlang, and the orchestrator's own check (3 independent reporters). Derived/labelled severity disagree (architect labelled SHOULD, but this is a policy floor per CLAUDE.md's 'a broken build or test leg this change introduced' clause) -- floor governs.

trigger: operator reads docs/user-manual/gateway.md's Distribution Cookie section to firewall a multi-node deployment, without reading the ADR
summary: The new inet_dist_listen_min/max (9100-9105) firewall range was undocumented in the operator-facing security section, despite ADR-2002 SS7b claiming it is documented there. Independently found by security-guardian and release-deploy; consistency-auditor (C-2) confirmed it was also absent from pki-architecture.md.

trigger: operator skims the gateway.md table of contents before reading the Gateway Clustering section body
summary: TOC entry for Gateway Clustering still read 'PLANNED' after the section body was updated to 'cluster FORMATION implemented'.

trigger: operator debugging why a container picked a surprising advertise address, with no user-manual pointer to the algorithm
summary: YUZU_GW_ADVERTISE_ADDR's 4-step auto-detection order (env var / DNS+interface-intersection / hostname / 127.0.0.1) was documented only in the entrypoint script's own comments, not in the user manual.

trigger: the node_up telemetry assertion in running_server_telemeters_nodeup_and_nodedown_test_ fails or times out
summary: Peer/PeerNode were bound inside the try block, so a failed node_up assertion left the after-clause unable to stop the peer, leaking a live distributed peer process for the rest of the eunit VM's lifetime. Fixed by binding before try and calling stop_peer/1 unconditionally in after.

trigger: the connect_failed telemetry counter's only exercising code path (do_tick_survives_an_unreachable_target_test_) runs with no assertion on the counter itself
summary: connect_failed had zero test coverage despite the shipped alert's remediation guidance leaning on it. Fixed by attaching a telemetry handler and asserting #{count => 1} fires.

trigger: a firewalled/silently-dropping peer is present in the resolved target list during a tick
summary: do_tick/1 dials peers sequentially via net_kernel:connect_node/1 with no per-call timeout; one unreachable peer can stretch a whole tick past the redial interval, delaying nodeup/nodedown processing. Independently raised by sre (Gate 3 F1) and unhappy-path (UP-7).

trigger: an operator scales the chisel/demo Docker image with docker compose --scale
summary: Dockerfile.gateway.chisel never wires the new gateway-entrypoint.sh and lacks dig/iproute2, so every chisel-image replica would advertise yuzu_gw@127.0.0.1 regardless of --scale, silently producing a non-functional mesh. Independently raised by release-deploy and gateway-erlang.

trigger: deploy/docker/gateway-entrypoint.sh's fallback chain changes behavior with no regression net
summary: The 4-step address-resolution fallback chain has zero automated test coverage. Bounded blast radius (single new shell script) -- SHOULD, not a policy floor.

trigger: a Compose-scaled replica is killed and a new different container is assigned the freed address within one redial tick or the net_ticktime nodedown window
summary: Node atoms are constructed purely from <short name>@<address> with no incarnation/instance discriminator; a reused address could in principle be treated as 'the same node reconnecting'. Synthesized as chaos scenario CH-1/CH-2. Not proven to cause misrouting (pg-group routing may be safe by node-atom identity alone) -- flagged for verification, not a proven defect. CORRECTED after linter catch: impact re-derived as I6 (unverified capability question), not I2 (confirmed corruption) -- architect's Gate 3 review found pg-group membership needs only a live connection with no extra handshake, and a dead peer's pid is cleaned up by process monitoring on disconnect, so misrouting was never empirically confirmed as reachable.

trigger: yuzu_gw_cluster_discovery crashes and restarts while a nodeup/nodedown transition occurs in the re-subscription gap
summary: A nodeup/nodedown firing between the old process's death and the restarted process's monitor_nodes(true) re-subscription is not queued and is permanently lost from the discrete node_up/node_down telemetry counter (the peers_connected gauge self-corrects on the next tick since it's a live nodes() query). Synthesized as chaos scenario CH-3.

trigger: a hand-edited (non-env-var) sys.config sets a non-integer cluster_redial_interval_ms, bypassing apply_env_overrides/0's try/catch
summary: init/1 does not validate cluster_redial_interval_ms; a malformed hand-edited value would crash send_after on the first tick and could exhaust yuzu_gw_sup's one_for_one restart intensity (10/60), escalating to killing sibling children (registry, health, telemetry). The reachable env-var path is closed (try/catch). Independently raised by unhappy-path (UP-12) and sre (F7).

trigger: a DNS resolution failure or peer connect failure occurs before Prometheus/Grafana is wired up for a fresh rollout
summary: yuzu_gw_cluster_discovery.erl had zero logger calls (telemetry-only), unlike every sibling gateway retry/reconnect module and inconsistent with the shell-side entrypoint script's own verbose logging in the same PR. Fixed with a bounded logger:warning naming failed targets and a logger:debug on DNS lookup failure.

trigger: an operator sets YUZU_GW_ALLOW_DEFAULT_COOKIE=1 with a genuinely custom but short (<32 char) cookie
summary: The override warning conflated 'known default' with 'custom-but-too-short', risking an operator not realizing their short cookie remains exploitable via the new DNS-dial-out brute-force oracle. Fixed to name which condition(s) triggered. CORRECTED after linter catch: impact re-derived as I8 (degraded-but-correct diagnostic clarity) -- the override mechanism and cookie-floor check enforce identically before/after; only the log message's specificity improved, no control silently failed either way.

trigger: YUZU_GW_SEED_NODES is set but every entry is empty/whitespace after trimming (stray comma, blank entries)
summary: A malformed YUZU_GW_SEED_NODES silently fell through to DNS discovery instead of the intended static topology, with only a generic info line. Fixed with a distinct warning.

trigger: an operator with an existing single-node gateway deployment and tooling hardcoding the old yuzu_gw1@127.0.0.1 node name upgrades
summary: The node short-name change (yuzu_gw1 -> yuzu_gw) affects every existing deployment's external tooling (remsh/recon/health checks), not just cluster adopters, but carried no Breaking changelog framing or upgrading.md callout. Fixed with Breaking prefixes on both changelog fragments and a new upgrading.md section.

trigger: an operator reads docs/user-manual/upgrading.md's breaking-changes ledger before upgrading, expecting parity with the existing #659 entry
summary: The 32-char cookie floor (extending #659) had no upgrading.md entry despite being a boot-time-breaking change for a short custom cookie. Fixed with a new section alongside #659.

trigger: a persistently misconfigured seed DNS name causes every node in a large cluster to query it every 5s indefinitely
summary: No-backoff DNS retry means query volume scales linearly with cluster size; undocumented for an operator sizing a large cluster against shared DNS infrastructure. Design tradeoff, not a defect. Fixed with a caveat paragraph.

trigger: an operator sizes a gateway fleet without knowing the inet_dist_listen_min/max range caps concurrent nodes
summary: The 6-port range (9100-9105) caps a cluster at 6 nodes today; not stated as a hard ceiling anywhere an operator sizing a fleet would see it. Fixed as part of the same firewall-ports paragraph.

trigger: yuzu_gw_cluster_formation_multinode_tests.erl is run in true module isolation with no earlier sibling test module having started the telemetry application
summary: The two telemetry-based tests rely on the telemetry app already being started by an earlier sibling test module in the shared EUnit VM; run in isolation they crash with {noproc, telemetry_handler_table}. Pre-existing pattern, not newly introduced, but the Gate 7 fix added one more test depending on it. Found during Gate 8 re-review.

trigger: a peer stays unreachable across many consecutive redial ticks (persistent firewall/partition)
summary: The new connect-failure logger:warning (added this round to fix the zero-logging finding) has no dedup/backoff on the log call itself; a sustained outage produces one line per 5s per affected node indefinitely. Bounded per-tick, unbounded in duration. Independently raised by sre (NICE) and unhappy-path (SHOULD) during Gate 8 re-review of the fix that introduced this logging.

trigger: N/A -- unreachable by construction (IsDefault and TooShort cannot both be true, since TooShort = not IsDefault andalso ...)
summary: The new Reason case's {true,true} clause ('...AND...') is unreachable dead code -- harmless, dialyzer-clean (dialyzer cannot correlate the two booleans' derivations), zero behavioral difference. Independently confirmed by security-guardian and gateway-erlang during Gate 8 re-review.

trigger: N/A -- Docker EXPOSE is documentation-only metadata with no functional/security effect (no -P is used by the new reference rig)
summary: EXPOSE was not extended to the new 9100-9105 distribution range or 4369/epmd. Purely metadata; the existing Dockerfile already omitted EPMD pre-PR. Declined as not worth a further edit-and-reverify cycle for a non-functional annotation.

trigger: an operator deliberately sets a 32-codepoint cookie of low-entropy or non-ASCII content, deviating from the documented openssl rand -hex 32 guidance
summary: The 32-char floor is length-only, not entropy-based; a low-entropy-but-32-char cookie clears the guard. Documented guidance (openssl rand -hex 32) already clears the floor with large margin. Independently noted by security-guardian and unhappy-path (UP-5). No code path found that would actually break; a documented-guidance gap, not a code defect.

trigger: a compromised or misconfigured DNS resolver returns an address outside the intended cluster trust boundary
summary: A foreign node could in principle join the mesh if it also knows/brute-forces the cookie; this is a design-acknowledged residual explicitly named in ADR-2002 SS7b, mitigated by the cookie floor, with -proto_dist inet_tls migration explicitly deferred as documented future work. Not a silent gap. CORRECTED after linter catch: exposure re-derived as E6 (wrong outcome proven unable to occur), not E4 -- security-guardian computed the specific brute-force oracle this finding names is computationally infeasible against a 32+ char cookie (~10^16 years at an unrealistic 10^15 hash/s), which caps the band at LOW per the E6 rule rather than leaving it at the I1 base.

trigger: N/A -- pre-existing documentation drift, confirmed present on origin/dev before this PR
summary: The numbered child-list doc comment omitted pg_scope and yuzu_gw_gauge before this PR; this PR's renumbering of the new cluster_discovery child is internally correct relative to what it inherited. Pre-existing, out of scope for this fix.

trigger: N/A -- pre-existing documentation drift in a comment-only header list
summary: The header's docker-compose.uat.yml gateway row doesn't match current tree state (that compose file has no gateway service). Predates this PR; out of scope here.

trigger: an auditor reviews docs/enterprise-readiness-soc2-first-customer.md expecting per-PR itemization of HA-program availability work
summary: Workstream D is written at a principle level and does not itemize individual HA-program PRs; every prior HA WS-0/1/3 slice also merged without touching this doc. Consistent with existing project convention, not a gap this PR introduces. Recommend the doc pick up a gateway-HA capability line at a future customer-facing milestone (program-level follow-up, not a per-PR blocker).

trigger: N/A -- pre-existing document drift predating the entire ADR-2002 HA program (WS-0 through WS-4), not specific to this PR
summary: SS14.6 describes an active-passive shared-SQLite-over-NFS HA model, stale relative to the whole Postgres-coordination HA program. Pre-existing, out of scope for this PR.

classification_rationale: the pass-1 row's E6 derivation conflated 'infeasible if the operator followed cookie-length guidance' with 'the wrong outcome proven unable to occur' -- SKILL.md's E6 requires the latter, and the same ledger's own 4555.cookie-length-not-entropy row concedes a low-entropy-but-32-char cookie clears the length floor while remaining weak, so the wrong outcome is NOT proven unable to occur. The correct exposure is E4 (a non-default condition -- an operator choosing a low-entropy cookie despite the length guidance), which SKILL.md states explicitly is NOT a downgrade. Honest re-derivation is I1 (base HIGH) + E4 (no change) = HIGH, mapped BLOCKING -- the pass-1 row's severity_mapped of NICE does not survive the corrected exposure.
summary: Re-derived after Fable's final pre-push review caught the pass-1 row's own E6-vs-E4 conflation. This is now recorded HONESTLY at its derived BLOCKING band rather than downgraded to fit a NICE disposition. It is REJECTED anyway, per Gate 7's stricter standard for rejecting a derived CRITICAL/HIGH finding (an adjudicator independent of the author, recorded below): the residual is a design-ACKNOWLEDGED trade-off, stated in full in ADR-2002 SS7b's own text (a CIDR/RFC1918 allow-list was explicitly considered and rejected there as the wrong control; -proto_dist inet_tls is named there as the durable fix, explicitly deferred as a follow-up, not silently dropped). The floor enforces length, not entropy, because entropy cannot be verified from a bare string -- the mitigation this PR ships (32-char minimum, openssl-rand-hex-32 guidance, all shipped packaging mints exactly that) is the practical, honest ceiling available at THIS layer, and going further (mandating a specific generation method, or verifying character-class distribution) was judged disproportionate to a threat that ALSO requires the attacker to already control DNS resolution for this specific seed name. The gap is real, named, and has a tracked durable fix (-proto_dist inet_tls) deferred to its own follow-up rather than blocking this PR. (reporter_ref: unresolved -- Fable's review was delivered as an in-session subagent hand-back, not a URL/PR-comment/committed transcript; no retrievable third-party artifact exists for this specific review pass.)
adjudicated_by: Fable (enterprise-architect, final pre-push review -- independent of this PR's author)
adjudication_rationale: Per Gate 7's rejection standard for a derived CRITICAL/HIGH finding: the claim is not false (the residual gap is real), but it is judged ADEQUATELY MITIGATED AND ALREADY DOCUMENTED as a deliberate design trade-off with a named durable follow-up (-proto_dist inet_tls), rather than an unaddressed defect. Independent adjudication by Fable, who was dispatched specifically to adversarially re-review this PR's severity derivations and was not involved in authoring the original finding, the original ledger row, or this PR's implementation.

trigger: the standard `rebar3 eunit --dir apps/yuzu_gw/test` full-suite invocation this project's CI actually runs -- NOT module isolation as the pass-1 governance row (4555.multinode-tests-telemetry-order-dependency) assumed
summary: Reproduced live on CI on both Linux and Windows legs (Failed: 3 on both) and locally by the reviewer, independent of the earlier governance-run report of the same underlying crash shape. The pass-1 ledger row's own trigger ('run in true module isolation') was empirically false -- it fails in the ordinary full-suite run CI uses, which is why it was deferred as non-blocking instead of fixed. Fixed: each telemetry-based test now calls application:ensure_all_started(telemetry) before attaching (ensure_telemetry_started/0 helper), matching the existing yuzu_gw_authz_tests.erl precedent.
classification_rationale: supersedes 4555.multinode-tests-telemetry-order-dependency's mis-stated trigger with the correct one

trigger: a hostile or misconfigured DNS answer for the configured seed name returns many distinct, individually-well-formed A-records, rotating on each 5s redial tick, forever (no backoff)
summary: Independently found by TWO parties: Fable's pre-push design review (filed as issue #4601, initially mis-scoped non-blocking P2) and FortitudeEtc's PR review (empirically reproduced: 10,000 distinct addresses -> +10,000 permanent atoms, no reclaim, OTP 28.4.2), which correctly escalated it to BLOCKING -- Erlang atoms are never garbage-collected, and this is reachable with NO cookie knowledge at all (a strictly easier attack than the cookie-brute-force scenario the MIN_COOKIE_LENGTH hardening already treats as in-scope threat model). Fixed: new sanitize_addrs/1 (validates each address via inet:parse_ipv4_address/1, dedupes, caps at 64) is now the single chokepoint both the DNS and static-override paths funnel through before any list_to_atom/1 call. Issue #4601 closed as fixed-in-PR rather than left as a deferred follow-up.

trigger: an unrelated distribution connection exists (a stale node still holding the cluster cookie, a dev shell left connected) that is not in the current tick's own resolved/configured target list
summary: peers_connected counted a bare length(nodes()) rather than being scoped to ExternalTargets, so an unrelated inbound connection could mask a genuinely failed seed peer (YuzuGatewayClusterPartiallyFormed's resolved-connected>0 alert staying clear when it shouldn't). Fixed: peers_connected now counts length([T || T <- ExternalTargets, lists:member(T, nodes())]). Regression test added (do_tick_scopes_peers_connected_to_targets_test_, two real peers, only one a target). (impact corrected I3->I6 after linter catch: this degrades the alert's DETECTION reliability in a narrow race, not the correctness of any user-facing/persisted data -- I6 base MEDIUM + E5 no-change = MEDIUM/SHOULD, not the I3-derived HIGH the first-pass row wrongly implied.)

trigger: an operator sets YUZU_GW_CLUSTER_REDIAL_INTERVAL_MS to 0 or a negative value
summary: 0 hot-loops DNS lookups every tick; a negative value raises badarg in erlang:send_after/3. Fixed: clamped to a 1000ms floor (max(RawInterval, 1000)) in init/1.

trigger: a hand-edited sys.config sets cluster_seed_nodes using plain Erlang strings (e.g. ["10.0.0.1"]) instead of binaries
summary: binary_to_list(A) crashed this gen_server on every tick if A was a plain string rather than a binary -- the YUZU_GW_SEED_NODES env-override path always produces binaries, but a hand-edited sys.config in ordinary Erlang string style is equally valid config syntax. Fixed: new addr_to_string/1 accepts both is_binary and is_list forms. (severity_mapped corrected NICE->SHOULD after linter catch: I5 (crash/unavailability) base MEDIUM + E4 no-change = MEDIUM/SHOULD, not NICE -- a LOW severity_native label doesn't override the honestly-derived band.)

trigger: n/a -- a static comment, not a runtime condition
summary: The comment claimed the 32-char MIN_COOKIE_LENGTH floor 'matches' openssl rand -hex 32's output, but that command emits 64 hex characters -- the floor is HALF the recommended generator's output, not equal to it. Functionally harmless (the floor is still comfortably cleared), but could mislead a future reader into weakening the floor or the guidance. Fixed: reworded to state the floor is half the recommended generator's length and to name the length-vs-entropy residual explicitly (a low-entropy 32-char string still clears a length-only check).

trigger: any change to yuzu_gw_cluster_discovery.erl or deploy/docker/gateway-entrypoint.sh
summary: This rig is the ONLY one that can exercise the fixed-short-name/IP-literal topology (the automated eunit multinode suite explicitly cannot on one shared EPMD host) -- but it pulls a previously-published image, not the PR's own build, and nothing in CI runs it. The property the whole #4555 feature leans on is unverified by any automated gate. Deferred (not blocking, per the reviewer's own framing): filed as issue #4612 (a scripts/ha/ verification script + CI wiring).
